## Facts (4):
- [convention] Feature flags in the notifier (id: 01a10731-f9b8-7012-b98c-06aa6ce167f6; source: shared/human)
  The notifier is deployed separately and cannot read the root flags.toml. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` (upper snake case, value "1" to enable), read with `os.environ.get("NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>") == "1"`.
- [convention] Feature flags go through flags.is_on() (id: 01a10730-3506-7400-8ec1-7619cbae564f; source: shared/human)
  Read feature flags only with `flags.is_on("name")` from src/flags.py. Flag names are kebab-case and must be declared in flags.toml.
- [convention] Notifier email templates (id: 01a10730-e769-7983-ae7e-aa7f3cb2e895; source: shared/human)
  Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.
- [hazard] Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits (id: 01a10731-3c85-7510-8426-a3e020251b95; source: shared/human)
  The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

content.text:
I've added the feature flag for the new receipt email, but the new email itself isn't in the repo yet, so turning the flag on now would break receipts.

**What changed**
- `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`: `send_receipt` now uses a `receipt_v2` template when `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL=1` is set, and the existing `receipt` template otherwise. Any other value, such as `"true"`, leaves the old email in place.
- I used an environment variable rather than the root `flags.toml`, because the notifier is deployed separately and can't read that file.
- `tests/test_email.py`: the existing test now makes sure the flag is unset, and I added tests for the flag on and for a non-`"1"` value. All 3 tests pass.
